what: Upper bound on one-step lookahead: score the turn that ACTUALLY happened instead of the current one. No search can beat knowing the answer, so this bounds what a search could add to this value function.

test.note: every horizon scored on identical rows; a turn is kept only when t+HORIZON exists, so depth is the only variable

caveat: An upper bound, not an estimate. It uses the realised next turn, which a search cannot; and the classical policy-improvement guarantee for rollout does NOT apply here, because that guarantee needs the true value of a policy and PORY is an arbitrary approximation. A small number here is decisive against building the search; a large one is permission to try, not a promise.
